# COMPLEMENT DEFICIENCY

Complement deficiency can be inherited or acquired. Acquired defects are usually a consequence of other diseases like systemic lupus erythematosus.
Complement deficiency leads to increased rates of infections, usually of the upper respiratory tract, but also occasionally with bacteremia or meningitis.
Pathogens are usually Streptococcus pneumoniae, Neisseria meningitidis, and Neisseria gonorrhea.
Patients presenting with fever or other symptoms suggesting systemic bacterial infection should be treated immediately with antimicrobials active against these pathogens.

[References](references)
Rich RR et al, eds. Clinical Immunology
Roitt I et al, eds. Immunology
Therapy:
## Preferred empirical treatment

Ceftriaxone 2 gm IV q24h ($5.71/day) [M]

## Alternative for severe penicillin allergy

Chloramphenicol is not currently available. Contact Infectious Diseases for advice.
